receipt.notes:
Worktree verified: toplevel == cwd, branch worktree-wf_abd0dbec-e89-2. Only the three target files were created; nothing else touched.

Referee points: (1) timeout is real wall clock -- judge() runs the SDK call on a plain threading.Thread(daemon=True) feeding a concurrent.futures.Future, then future.result(timeout=TIMEOUT_S=0.8); the test measures time.perf_counter() around the call against a 5 s sleeping fake. (2) No path raises out of judge(): inner try/except covers TimeoutError + concurrent.futures.TimeoutError + Exception; an outer try/except Exception wraps the whole body (covers non-dict questions, bad mode, ledger failure). Ledger writes themselves swallow all errors. (3) Ledger path: ~/.synapse/jev/<lane>.jsonl by default (lane sanitized to [A-Za-z0-9-_.]); SYNAPSE_JEV_LEDGER_DIR env overrides the root; test_default_ledger_root_is_under_home_synapse_jev pins the default. (4) Boundary: python/synapse/jev contains no 'harness', 'jev_client', etc.; the docstring cites 'invariant 5 of the Jev README' and 'the build-time question builder' by description rather than path, since the boundary regex and the acceptance grep both forbid the literal.

Design notes: SDK access is one module-level seam, _load_sdk(), so tests inject a fake TypeSafeClient + Choice/Score/Noul classes with zero network; call shape mirrors the harness client (client.system_one(state=, questions=, model=) with TypeError fallback for older SDKs). Disabled short-circuits before the ledger too, so an OFF product writes nothing anywhere. The main-thread check uses sys.modules.get('hou') so the adapter never imports hou itself. Environment note: this box runs Python 3.14.2 (conftest warns the vendored cp311/cp313 wheels are inactive); that warning is pre-existing and unrelated to this leg. No callers were added, per the mission.

receipt.notes:
Design choices worth a referee's eye:
1. Decision protocol in guard-edit-targets.py: allow = exit 0 + zero bytes (verified with od -c: byte-identical to the original); policy deny = exit 0 + JSON permissionDecision=deny (unchanged protocol); fail-closed = exit 2 (DENY_EXIT) + reason on stderr + JSON deny on stdout. Exit 2 is Claude Code's blocking code, so a broken/malformed fire is refused even if the JSON is ignored. Fail-closed is a real try/except around the whole main() with decision defaulting to deny; pinned by 6 malformed-input shapes plus a test that a broken ledger path cannot flip the decision either way.
2. Worktree fence is checked BEFORE the pattern list, so a worktree cwd gets the specific 'Worktree fence' reason even when the path would also hit AppData/houdini prefs. Main-tree cwd behaviour is unchanged. Fence uses JSON `cwd` when present, else os.getcwd(); relative paths resolve against cwd; sibling worktrees count as outside.
3. _ledger.py has zero decisions (test scans the code body for sys.exit / permissionDecision / synapse.log / harness). It is force-added: .gitignore:75 (`_*.py`) would hide it; .gitignore was outside my targets so I did not edit it -- someone may want a `!.claude/hooks/_ledger.py` exception. Ledger path override: SYNAPSE_HOOKS_LEDGER env; session from hook JSON session_id, else CLAUDE_SESSION_ID env.
4. check-python.sh stays bash with an inline `python -c` shim (stdin passed via herestring); exit stays 0; decisions recorded: ok / syntax_error / skip / error:<Type>. Smoke-tested live on a real syntax-error file: message printed, exit 0, ledger row syntax_error.
5. Bridge: additive _run() wrapper + _LAST_HOOK bookkeeping in main(); no bridge fire removed, no exit code changed.
6. Not done / caveats: settings.json still points at the MAIN-tree copy of the hooks (python C:/Users/User/SYNAPSE/.claude/hooks/...), so the new behaviour goes live only once this branch merges into master. The worktree fence is exercised by subprocess tests with fictional paths because pytest's tmp_path is under AppData on Windows (already denied by the pattern list). ~/.synapse/hooks.jsonl was never written by tests (env override throughout).
